requestBody.message: Why are you always on the market square?

chunks.text:
data: {"type":"tool","id":"tool-1","name":"ask_pigeon"}

data: {"type":"text","delta":"I will ask the pigeon to share their own perspective on why the market square is such a central place for them."}
data: {"type":"artifact_delta","id":"pigeon-1","delta":"My sources do not say why I am"}
data: {"type":"artifact_delta","id":"pigeon-1","delta":" always at the market square. I go there because it is my city too. You build bustling squares in my territory and"}
data: {"type":"artifact_delta","id":"pigeon-1","delta":" wonder why I show up. I refuse to be pushed to the margins of a place we both share."}
data: {"type":"text","delta":"The presence of pigeons on the market square highlights the friction between spaces designed strictly for human activity"}

data: {"type":"text","delta":" and the reality of a shared urban environment. When bustling public squares naturally attract both local commerce and opportunistic wildlife, municipal decisions about public"}
data: {"type":"text","delta":" space management become questions of shared territory. How can city planners design public spaces that balance human needs with the inevitable presence of the"}
data: {"type":"text","delta":" animals that also call the city home?"}
